findings.title: Meeting artifact writes accept arbitrary success bodies and discard the editor
findings.reproduction: Open client Calendar meeting, Notes, Add note; type a draft; intercept POST response200 with {saved:false,meetingId:"foreign-meeting",clientId:"foreign-client"}; leave GET notes unchanged. Save closes the editor, loses the draft, and no new note appears. z.unknown is also used by edit/approve/share/unshare; new browser reproduction is for note creation.
findings.deploymentImpact: Blocks acceptance of these mutation paths as receipt-verified. Frontend repair can validate the existing metadata and preserve uncertain draft. Does not establish a backend authorization bypass or require a blanket static-preview deployment hold.
findings.backendContractComparison: Pinned backend fd8765ec01d292013758606204f2c9d886cd31c1 createMeetingNote5696,createMeetingDebrief5794 and metadata selects10836/10858 return id,meetingId,clientId,author,status,timestamps. This is available validation data, not a missing receipt contract.

findings.title: Meeting note/debrief creation can replay after an uncertain result and dispatch twice
findings.reproduction: Intercept note creation with503. Save remains enabled, a second click emits a second POST with the same body. After it settles, two synchronous submit events emit two further POSTs. Mutation contains no synchronous pending ref, attempt key or uncertain completion fence; disabling the rendered button is insufficient. Debrief shares this hook but was not independently dispatched in this review.
findings.deploymentImpact: Blocks claiming reliable note/debrief creation under retries; potentially duplicates saved records after response loss. No live record was created. Backend idempotency would be additional protection; frontend can immediately refuse blind replay.
findings.backendContractComparison: Pinned backend creation directly calls meetingNote.create/meetingDebrief.create and exposes no idempotency input in this contract. It does not deduplicate repeat POSTs for the frontend.

findings.title: Clearing a meeting location never clears the saved value
findings.reproduction: Open a meeting with location, Edit meeting, clear Location or join URL, Save. Payload lacks location and the prior value remains. New fixture control captures the omitted field and unchanged location.
findings.deploymentImpact: Blocks the clear-location part of edit acceptance; localized frontend fix. No deployment-wide dependency.
findings.backendContractComparison: Pinned backend updateMeeting1528 updates location only when the property exists and treats empty string/null as clearing. It deliberately preserves omitted fields.

findings.title: Meeting save accepts a receipt for a different meeting/client
findings.reproduction: During Edit meeting, return a schema-valid meeting with id="other-meeting" and client.id="foreign-client". Editor closes as successful; unlike useMeeting read validation, useSaveMeeting checks only broad meeting shape. The new control combines this with location-clear payload inspection.
findings.deploymentImpact: Blocks receipt-context acceptance of meeting saves. New browser proof is edit; create uses the same hook and needs expected submitted-client checks. No server ACL bypass was shown.
findings.backendContractComparison: Existing meeting response includes id and client; frontend has original meetingId and selected client available to compare. Backend contract expansion is not required for those checks.

findings.title: Client Agenda omits lifecycle triage filters and state columns
findings.reproduction: Open client Calendar Agenda. Only search, Meeting visibility and Clear filters appear; there are no Needs prep/Needs debrief controls. Generic cards show status/provenance, but no Prep, Meeting notes and Debrief columns. Compare new screenshot with captured frame411:63431.
findings.deploymentImpact: Prevents the designed meeting triage workflow and full visual acceptance. It is a frontend parity gap; native auth/provider availability cannot resolve it.

findings.title: Meeting workspace loses identity context across tabs and always enters Information
findings.reproduction: Open completed meeting. Information is always active. Switch Notes: date/time, location and attendee display disappear; only subject/privacy/client remain. Figma keeps ID/lifecycle status/date/attendees above tabs and its component context specifies upcoming→Prep/live→Notes/completed→Debrief. The captured completed frame itself shows a Notes state, so this finding does not claim a single mandatory tab from its pixels alone.
findings.deploymentImpact: Meeting details exist but full designed workspace parity is not accepted. Local presentation/routing work; no backend contract blocker.

findings.title: Saved email signature is fetched but never displayed
findings.reproduction: Return a nonempty enabled signature from GET me/email-signature, open New email. Append checkbox is checked but saved signature text is absent from composer and review; generic explanation replaces the preview. Figma child context has Automatic email signature/Saved signature text.
findings.deploymentImpact: Cannot accept Display saved user email signature; reviewer cannot inspect appended identity content. Sending transport may still work. Frontend display repair; no new backend needed.
findings.backendContractComparison: The current GET contract already provides html and enabled. Figma child screenshots are1x1 because composer is clipped/off-canvas; structured child context is preserved and no pixel-level comparison is claimed.

findings.title: Prep and attachment share/unshare are missing
findings.reproduction: Inspect meeting preparation and attachment controls. Prep can be read/refined/exported/emailed; attachment can be reviewed/approved. Only note/debrief artifact changes build share/unshare requests. No prep/attachment branch or selection exists in Portfolio Calendar.
findings.deploymentImpact: Two rows are partially implemented, not wholly unavailable: note/debrief operations exist, prep/attachment facets do not. These missing controls block full artifact sharing acceptance; feature flag/provider-native acceptance remains separate.
findings.backendContractComparison: Pinned controller2089/2098 exposes per-artifact share/unshare. Existing contract has target artifact list; no need to invent whole-meeting sharing, which remains excluded.

findings.title: Client-shared meeting materials feed has no Portfolio consumer
findings.reproduction: Search current Portfolio source for shared-meetings and inspect feed/library owners: no consumer exists. The standard Calendar GET and caller-owned approved library do not replace the separate client-shared feed.
findings.deploymentImpact: Blocks this read criterion specifically. Existing service contract is available; remaining work is frontend composition plus native authorization evidence.
findings.backendContractComparison: Pinned controller2383 exposes GET engagement/shared-meetings?clientId for client-shared materials, distinct from caller-owned archive.

findings.title: Email composer omits the designed rich-text formatting controls
findings.reproduction: Open New email. Message is a textarea; no Bold/Italic/Underline/List formatting toolbar exists. Figma child context explicitly contains these controls, while plainMailHtml escapes plain text into paragraphs.
findings.deploymentImpact: Visual/editor capability gap, not proof that plain-text email delivery fails. Do not use it as a blanket deployment hold. Child render is clipped; exact pixel parity unassessed.

findings.title: Meri rewrite has no Undo control or prior-body snapshot
findings.reproduction: A verified rewrite replaces body. Hook exposes only body/edit/rewrite and stores no previous body; composer has no Undo rewrite action. Captured Figma child includes an Undo Meri rewrite variant. This is source/design-context evidence, not a paid rewrite execution.
findings.deploymentImpact: Rewrite request/response behavior is implemented; the designed undo facet is absent. Local parity work and not a provider deployment dependency.
